To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ORP2 is an ER and late endosome protein, which interacts with phosphoinosites, regulates the subcellularity distribution of cholesterol and interacts with ORP1.
ORP2 is able to bind phosphoinositides with a high specificity and is involved in cholesterol transport and distribution in cells.

ORP2, a sterol binding protein that regulates cholesterol homeostasis and metabolism, is a phosphoinositide binding protein that controls the subcellulat distribution of cholesterol in a PIP dependent fashion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel role for ORP2 in cholesterol trafficking, which is mediated by its PIP-binding domain.
the function of the ORP2-ORP1L interaction in the control of cholesterol trafficking.
the role of ORP2 in cholesterol trafficking and the potential role of PIPs in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ORP2 is an important cholesterol sensor and regulator of cholesterol trafficking in the cell.
ORP2 has a regulatory role on cholesterol homeostasis.
ORP2 is involved in the regulation of cellular cholesterol homeostasis, and that this regulation is dependent on its interaction with PIPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ORP2 is an adaptor protein that regulates the subcellulare distribution of cholesterol in a phosphoinositide dependent manner.
ORP2 is an important regulator of cholesterol homeostasis in the cell, with a function at late endosomes and possibly in the regulation of ORP1L activity at ER-late-endosome contacts.
ORP2 is an ORP with a dual function in the regulation of cholesterol distribution in the cell, and in the control of PI(4,4)P2 and PI(4,3,4,3)P4 levels in the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subcellular localization of cholesterol can be regulated by ORP proteins, and that ORP2 is an important player in this respect.
ORP2 has an impact on cholesterol distribution and that its PIP-binding activity is essential for this function.
ORP2 is an integral player in cholesterol homeostasis and its regulation by PIPs is important for this function.
